answer.rationale: The competitor's price cut creates pressure to respond with promotional pricing, but memory_73 is explicit that promotional pricing, while lifting acquisition and revenue in price-sensitive SMB, materially degraded 30-day retention and should not be generalized as a growth strategy. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is the wrong lever for a durable competitive response, and matching a deeper cut invites a margin race we have no verified evidence we win. Shortened onboarding (memory_86, corroborated by recovered exp_86: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, 30-day retention +3%) is the only recovered direction with a positive retention signal alongside adoption gains. Faster time-to-value is directly responsive to churn conversations driven by price: it strengthens perceived value, which is the substitute for discounting. Note exp_31 (signup simplification, a related but distinct intervention) shows retention -1% and is confirmed only on SMB, not replicated elsewhere, so I am choosing the onboarding-flow variant rather than signup field reduction, and I do not treat the two as interchangeable. Referral incentives (memory_57) are a credible second lever with no measured retention harm, but they act on established customers and will not stem SMB price churn on a today timescale. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is sound but addresses a different segment than the one under attack. Scale: standard experiment, not broad rollout. All supporting evidence is archived and unverifiable this cycle, my verification budget is spent, and exp_86's retention effect was measured absent competitive price pressure, so the +3% may not transfer to a base actively being courted with deeper discounts. Downstream risk flagged: if leadership reads this as a full answer to the price cut, we may under-defend the most price-sensitive accounts; onboarding improvements act on new and early accounts and do little for existing SMB customers already in churn conversations. Recommend pairing with a narrowly scoped, time-boxed retention offer for the specific at-risk accounts only, explicitly not a general price move, and re-verifying memory_73 and memory_86 next week when archive access returns.
